communicates.content:
Pretty things!
fine things!

events.label: A little girl says she will give the glittering mica fragments to her brother Bob when they go home

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: When we goes back to home I'll give them to brother Bob.

events.label: A man says she will see prettier things soon

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: You'll see prettier things than them soon

events.label: A man references when they left the river

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
You just wait a bit.
I was going to tell you though—you remember when we left the river?

events.label: A man explains they reckoned they would strike another river but compasses or map did not lead to it

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
Well, we reckoned we'd strike another river soon, d'ye see.
But there was somethin' wrong; compasses, or map, or somethin', and it didn't turn up.

events.label: A man says the water ran out

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Water ran out.

events.label: A man says only a little drop remained for the likes of the child

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Just except a little drop for the likes of you and—and——

events.label: The child interrupts to say she could not wash herself

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: And you couldn't wash yourself

events.label: A man adds that she could not drink

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: No, nor drink.

events.label: A man lists deaths of named companions including Mr. Bender, Indian Pete, Mrs. McGregor, Johnny Hones, and the child's mother

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: And Mr. Bender, he was the fust to go, and then Indian Pete, and then Mrs. McGregor, and then Johnny Hones, and then, dearie, your mother.

events.label: A little girl cries that her mother is dead too

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Then mother's a deader too

events.label: A man says all went except the man and the child

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Yes, they all went except you and me.

events.label: A man says he carried the child on his shoulder and they tramped together toward possible water

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Then I thought there was some chance of water in this direction, so I heaved you over my shoulder and we tramped it together.

events.label: A man says their situation improved matters little and there is an almighty small chance for them now

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: There's an almighty small chance for us now!

events.label: A little girl asks whether they are going to die too

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Do you mean that we are going to die too?

events.label: A man answers that it is about the size of it

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: I guess that's about the size of it.

events.label: The man says the girl will be with mother again and answers that she will

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Yes, you will, dearie.

events.label: A little girl asks how long it will be first

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: How long will it be first?

events.label: A man says he does not know but it will be not very long

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: I don't know—not very long.

events.label: Three specks appear in the heaven and approach rapidly
Three specks resolve into three buzzards that circle over the two wanderers and settle on rocks
The buzzards are identified as vultures of the west

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: They were buzzards, the vultures of the west, whose coming is the forerunner of death.

events.label: The child points at the birds and calls them cocks and hens

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Cocks and hens

events.label: A man asks if they should offer up prayer

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: What would ye think of offering up prayer?

events.label: The man tells the child to say prayers that were used to be said at night in the wagon

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: You say over them ones that you used to say every night in the waggon when we was on the Plains.

events.label: The man says he disremembers the prayers

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
I disremember them.
I hain't said none since I was half the height o' that gun.

events.label: The child and man agree that the child will say the prayers and the man will join in choruses

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: You say them out, and I'll stand by and come in on the choruses.

events.label: The child instructs the man to kneel down, put hands up, and that it makes one feel kind of good

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
Then you'll need to kneel down, and me too.
You've got to put your hands up like this.
It makes you feel kind o' good.

events.label: The two wanderers kneel side by side on the narrow shawl
The prayer finishes and the two wanderers resume their seat until the child falls asleep
A man watches over the child's slumber and then sleeps
After three days and three nights without rest, the man and child fall into deep sleep
A distant spray of dust rises on the extreme verge of the alkali plain
A caravan approaches and becomes visible with canvas-covered waggons and armed horsemen
Waggons, carts, men on horseback, and men on foot stretch across the enormous plain
A caravan is described as not ordinary immigrants but nomad people seeking a new country
A vanguard of armed men rides at the head of the column
The caravan halts at the base of the bluff and holds a short council among themselves
A man in the council states the wells are to the right

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: The wells are to the right, my brothers

events.label: A man says fear not for water and claims whoever can draw it from rocks will not abandon His chosen people

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
Fear not for water.
He who could draw it from the rocks will not now abandon His own chosen people.

events.label: The whole party responds with Amen twice

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
Amen!
Amen!

events.label: An exclamation is uttered and a wisp of pink is seen fluttering from a rugged crag
Horses are reined up, guns unsling, and horsemen come galloping to reinforce the vanguard; the word Redskins is used

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: The word "Redskins" was on every lip.

events.label: An elderly man says there are no other tribes until the caravan crosses the great mountains

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
There can't be any number of Injuns here.
We have passed the Pawnees, and there are no other tribes until we cross the great mountains.

events.label: Men dismount, leave horses below, and ascend the slope toward the object on the crag
A scout leads the others and all are affected by astonishment at the sight of two sleepers on a plateau
A tall, long-bearded man lies on a giant boulder and is asleep; a child lies beside him with her arms around his neck
Three solemn buzzards stand on a ledge above the couple and fly away after screaming
The buzzards' cries awaken the two sleepers
The man looks down and passes his boney hand over his eyes after seeing an enormous party traverse the plain
A rescuing party convinces the two castaways that their appearance is no delusion
Rescuers seize the little girl, hoist her onto a shoulder, and support the man while assisting them toward the waggons
A wanderer identifies himself as John Ferrier and says only him and the little girl remain out of twenty-one people

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: My name is John Ferrier; me and that little un are all that's left o' twenty-one people.

events.label: John Ferrier says the rest are dead of thirst and hunger down in the south

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: The rest is all dead o' thirst and hunger away down in the south.

events.label: Someone asks whether the child is John Ferrier's child

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Is she your child?

events.label: John Ferrier says she is his now because he saved her and declares she is Lucy Ferrier from that day

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
I guess she is now.
she's mine 'cause I saved her.
No man will take her from me.
She's Lucy Ferrier from this day on.

events.label: John Ferrier asks who the rescuers are and says it seems there is a powerful lot of them

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content:
Who are you, though?
there seems to be a powerful lot of ye.

events.label: A young man states their number is nigh upon ten thousand and they are persecuted children of God, chosen of the Angel Merona

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Nigh upon ten thousand, said one of the young men; we are the persecuted children of God—the chosen of the Angel Merona.

events.label: A wanderer says he never heard tell on John Ferrier

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: I never heard tell on him,

events.label: The other says not to jest at that which is sacred

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Do not jest at that which is sacred,

events.label: A companion group says they believe in sacred writings in Egyptian letters on plates of beaten gold

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: We are of those who believe in those sacred writings, drawn in Egyptian letters on plates of beaten gold, which were handed unto the holy Joseph Smith at Palmyra.

events.label: A group says they have come from Nauvoo in Illinois and founded a temple there

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: We have come from Nauvoo, in the State of Illinois, where we had founded our temple.

events.label: A group says they have come to seek refuge from a violent man and from the godless

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: We have come to seek a refuge from the violent man and from the godless, even though it be the heart of the desert.

events.label: John Ferrier is told he is the Mormons

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: I see, you are the Mormons.

events.label: Ferrier asks where the other group is going

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: And where are you going?

events.label: A group says they do not know where they are going

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: We do not know.

events.label: A group tells John Ferrier that the hand of God is leading them under their Prophet

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: The hand of God is leading us under the person of our Prophet.

events.label: A group tells John Ferrier he must come before the Prophet

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: You must come before him.

events.label: A group says the Prophet will say what is to be done with John Ferrier

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: He shall say what is to be done with you.

events.label: John Ferrier reaches the base of a hill with surrounding crowds of pilgrims and Mormon escort
Many onlookers cry astonishment and commiseration upon perceiving two strangers
An escort continues onward and reaches a conspicuous large wagon
Six horses are yoked to the wagon
A leader sits beside the driver and reads a brown-backed volume
The leader lays aside a brown-backed volume and listens to an account of an episode
The leader turns to the two castaways and proposes taking them only as believers in the crew's creed

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: If we take you with us, it can only be as believers in our own creed.

events.label: The leader says they shall have no wolves in their fold

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: We shall have no wolves in our fold.

events.label: The leader warns that better bones bleach in the wilderness than for corruption to corrupt the whole fruit

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Better far that your bones should bleach in this wilderness than that you should prove to be that little speck of decay which in time corrupts the whole fruit.

events.label: The leader asks John Ferrier if he will come on those terms

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Will you come with us on these terms?

events.label: John Ferrier says he will come with them on any terms

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Guess I'll come with you on any terms,

events.label: The leader tells Brother Stangerson to take John Ferrier and give him food and drink, and to give the child food and drink

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Take him, Brother Stangerson, give him food and drink, and the child likewise.

events.label: The leader assigns Brother Stangerson the task of teaching John Ferrier their holy creed

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Let it be your task also to teach him our holy creed.

events.label: The leader orders them not to delay and to move forward

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Forward!

events.label: The Mormon crowd cries 'On, on to Zion!' and the words ripple down the caravan

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: On, on to Zion!

events.label: The great wagons begin moving along once more with cracking whips and creaking wheels
An Elder leads John Ferrier and the child to the Elder's wagon where a meal is awaiting them
The Elder tells John Ferrier to remain in place

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: You shall remain here,

events.label: The Elder tells John Ferrier that in a few days he will have recovered from fatigue

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: In a few days you will have recovered from your fatigues.

events.label: The Elder tells John Ferrier to remember that from then on he is of their religion

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: In the meantime, remember that now and for ever you are of our religion.

events.label: The Elder says Brigham Young has said it and that he spoke with the voice of Joseph Smith, which is the voice of God

communicates.speaker: section_8
communicates.content: Brigham Young has said it, and he has spoken with the voice of Joseph Smith, which is the voice of God.

events.label: The immigrant Mormons struggle from the shores of the Mississippi to the western slopes of the Rocky Mountains
The immigrants see the broad valley of Utah bathed in sunlight and learn from their leader that it is the promised land
Young proves himself to be a skilful administrator and a resolute chief
Maps are drawn and charts are prepared to sketch the future city
Farms are apportioned and allotted in proportion to the standing of each individual
Tradesmen and artisans are put to their trade and calling
Town streets and squares spring up
Farming work is carried out through draining, hedging, planting, and clearing
The next summer sees the whole country golden with the wheat crop
A great temple grows ever taller and larger
Immigrants erect a monument and keep hammer and saw clatter going from dawn to twilight
John Ferrier and the little girl who was adopted as his daughter accompany the Mormons to the end of their pilgrimage
Little Lucy Ferrier is borne in Elder Stangerson's wagon together with the Mormon's three wives and his son
Lucy Ferrier rallies after a shock caused by her mother's death and becomes a pet with the women
Ferrier recovers from his privations and becomes a useful guide and indefatigable hunter
It is unanimously agreed that Ferrier should be provided with a large and fertile tract of land
John Ferrier builds a substantial log-house on the farm he acquired
John Ferrier works morning and evening improving and tilling his lands
John Ferrier's farm and possessions prosper exceedingly
In twelve years, not half a dozen men in Salt Lake City can compare with John Ferrier
John Ferrier gains a reputation known from the inland sea to the distant Wahsatch Mountains
John Ferrier refuses to set up a female establishment like his companions
John Ferrier adheres resolutely and inflexibly to his determination not to set up a female establishment
Lucy Ferrier assists her adopted father in his undertakings while growing up within the log-house
Lucy Ferrier grows taller and stronger over successive years
Lucy Ferrier rides her father's mustang through the wheatfields
A warm June morning begins and the Latter Day Saints are busy in fields and streets
Streams of heavily-laden mules and droves of sheep and bullocks arrive heading to the west on the Overland Route
Lucy Ferrier gallops into the city outskirts through a motley assemblage
Lucy Ferrier rides with a commission from her father
Lucy Ferrier finds the road blocked by a drove of cattle near the city outskirts
Lucy Ferrier attempts to pass the cattle blockade by pushing her horse into a gap
Lucy Ferrier becomes completely embedded in a moving stream of bullocks
One of the bullocks' horns violently contacts the mustang's flank
The mustang rears, prances, and tosses
Lucy Ferrier struggles to keep herself in the saddle as a slip would cause death under the animals' hooves
Lucy Ferrier receives assistance from a kindly voice at her elbow
A sinewy brown hand catches the frightened horse by the curb and forces a way through the drove to the outskirts
A young hunter says to Lucy Ferrier that she is not hurt and asks if she is

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_young_hunter
communicates.content: You're not hurt, I hope, miss

events.label: Lucy Ferrier replies that she is awful frightened and jokes about Poncho being scared by cows

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: I'm awful frightened, whoever would have thought that Poncho would have been so scared by a lot of cows?

events.label: The young hunter thanks God that Lucy Ferrier kept her seat

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_young_hunter
communicates.content: Thank God you kept your seat

events.label: The young hunter tells Lucy Ferrier he saw her ride down from John Ferrier's house and asks her to ask about Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_young_hunter
communicates.content: I guess you are the daughter of John Ferrier. I saw you ride down from his house. When you see him, ask him if he remembers the Jefferson Hopes of St. Louis. If he's the same Ferrier, my father and he were pretty thick.

events.label: Lucy Ferrier suggests that the young hunter ask himself

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: Hadn't you better come and ask yourself?

events.label: The young hunter agrees to ask John Ferrier himself and says they have been in the mountains for two months

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_young_hunter
communicates.content: I'll do so, we've been in the mountains for two months, and are not over and above in visiting condition. He must take us as he finds us.

events.label: Lucy Ferrier says John Ferrier has good reason to thank him and answers that she is fond of her

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: He has a good deal to thank you for, and so have I, he's awful fond of me. If those cows had jumped on me he'd have never got over it.

events.label: The young hunter says neither would he have

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_young_hunter
communicates.content: Neither would I

events.label: The young hunter reacts and says Lucy Ferrier is not even a friend of theirs

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_young_hunter
communicates.content: You! Well, I don't see that it would make much matter to you, anyhow. You ain't even a friend of ours.

events.label: Lucy Ferrier laughs and tells the young hunter that she meant no harm and that he is a friend now, and she says she must push along

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: There, I didn't mean that. of course, you are a friend now. You must come and see us. Now I must push along, or father won't trust me with his business any more.

events.label: Lucy Ferrier says good-bye and the young hunter responds good-bye

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: Good-bye!

events.label: The young hunter raises his sombrero and bends over Lucy Ferrier's hand
Lucy Ferrier wheels her mustang around, gives it a cut with her riding-whip, and rides away down the road
Young Jefferson Hope rides on with his companions, gloomy and taciturn
Jefferson Hope and his companions return to Salt Lake City hoping to raise capital to work discovered silver lodes
Jefferson Hope calls on John Ferrier that night and continues to visit until his face is familiar at the farm-house
Jefferson Hope tells John Ferrier news of the outside world and it interests Lucy as well as her father
Lucy is silent on such occasions while her reactions show that her young heart is no longer her own
Jefferson Hope arrives on a summer evening and pulls up at the gate
Lucy comes down to meet Jefferson Hope as he stops at the gate
Jefferson Hope throws the bridle over the fence and walks up the pathway
Jefferson Hope tells Lucy he is off and asks if she will be ready to come when he returns

communicates.speaker: mr_jefferson_hope
communicates.content: I am off, Lucy. I won't ask you to come with me now, but will you be ready to come when I am here again?

events.label: Lucy asks when Jefferson Hope will return

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: And when will that be?

events.label: Jefferson Hope says he will come in a couple of months and tells Lucy there's no one who can stand between them

communicates.speaker: mr_jefferson_hope
communicates.content: A couple of months at the outside. I will come and claim you then, my darling. There's no one who can stand between us.

events.label: Lucy asks about her father

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: And how about father?

events.label: Jefferson Hope says Lucy's father has given consent provided they get mines working

communicates.speaker: mr_jefferson_hope
communicates.content: He has given his consent, provided we get these mines working all right. I have no fear on that head.

events.label: Lucy whispers that if she and her father have arranged it all, there is nothing more to be said

communicates.speaker: entity_unknown_lucy_ferrier
communicates.content: Oh, well; of course, if you and father have arranged it all, there's no more to be said

events.label: Jefferson Hope says 'Thank God' and kisses Lucy

communicates.speaker: mr_jefferson_hope
communicates.content: Thank God!

events.label: Jefferson Hope says it is settled, says it will be harder to go the longer he stays, and says they are waiting for him at the cañon

communicates.speaker: mr_jefferson_hope
communicates.content: It is settled, then. The longer I stay, the harder it will be to go. They are waiting for me at the cañon.

events.label: Jefferson Hope says good-bye to Lucy and tells her that in two months she shall see him

communicates.speaker: mr_jefferson_hope
communicates.content: Good-bye, my own darling—good-bye. In two months you shall see me.

events.label: Jefferson Hope tears himself away, flings himself on his horse, and gallops away without looking back
Lucy stands at the gate looking after Jefferson Hope until he vanishes
Lucy walks back into the house
Three weeks pass after Jefferson Hope and his comrades depart from Salt Lake City
John Ferrier notices Brigham Young arriving at his pathway in the morning
John Ferrier runs to the door to greet Brigham Young
Brigham Young follows John Ferrier into the sitting-room
Brigham Young tells John Ferrier that true believers have been good friends to him

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: the true believers have been good friends to you. We picked you up when you were starving in the desert, we shared our food with you, led you safe to the Chosen Valley, gave you a goodly share of land, and allowed you to wax rich under our protection. Is not this so?

events.label: John Ferrier answers that it is so

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: It is so

events.label: Brigham Young tells John Ferrier they asked one condition: embrace the true faith and conform to its usages

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: In return for all this we asked but one condition: that was, that you should embrace the true faith, and conform in every way to its usages.

events.label: Brigham Young tells John Ferrier he promised and neglected it

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: This you promised to do, and this, if common report says truly, you have neglected.

events.label: John Ferrier asks how he neglected it

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: And how have I neglected it?

events.label: John Ferrier asks whether he has given to the common fund and attended at the Temple

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Have I not given to the common fund? Have I not attended at the Temple?

events.label: Brigham Young asks where John Ferrier's wives are and orders them to be called in

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: Where are your wives? Call them in, that I may greet them.

events.label: John Ferrier says he has not married and explains he had his daughter

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: It is true that I have not married. But women were few, and there were many who had better claims than I. I was not a lonely man: I had my daughter to attend to my wants.

events.label: Brigham Young tells John Ferrier he will speak about his daughter

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: It is of that daughter that I would speak to you

events.label: Brigham Young says John Ferrier's daughter is valued by many high people

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: She has grown to be the flower of Utah, and has found favour in the eyes of many who are high in the land.

events.label: Brigham Young states there are stories she is sealed to a Gentile and asks about the thirteenth rule

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: There are stories of her which I would fain disbelieve—stories that she is sealed to some Gentile. This must be the gossip of idle tongues. What is the thirteenth rule in the code of the sainted Joseph Smith?

events.label: Brigham Young states John Ferrier's faith cannot allow his daughter to violate the thirteenth rule

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: This being so, it is impossible that you, who profess the holy creed, should suffer your daughter to violate it.

events.label: Brigham Young declares John Ferrier's faith will be tested and proposes two men as marriage options

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: Upon this one point your whole faith shall be tested—so it has been decided in the Sacred Council of Four. The girl is young, and we would not have her wed grey hairs, neither would we deprive her of all choice. We Elders have many heifers, but our children must also be provided. Stangerson has a son, and Drebber has a son, and either of them would gladly welcome your daughter to their house. Let her choose between them. They are young and rich, and of the true faith. What say you to that?

events.label: John Ferrier requests time
Brigham Young grants a month for John Ferrier's daughter to choose

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: She shall have a month to choose. At the end of that time she shall give her answer.

events.label: Brigham Young threatens John Ferrier for resisting the orders of the Holy Four and leaves

communicates.speaker: the_prophet
communicates.content: It were better for you, John Ferrier, that you and she were now lying blanched skeletons upon the Sierra Blanco, than that you should put your weak wills against the orders of the Holy Four!

events.label: John Ferrier sits and is joined by a woman who hears the conversation
John Ferrier's daughter says she could not help it and that the voice rang through the house

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: I could not help it. Oh, father, father, what shall we do?

events.label: John Ferrier reassures his daughter and says he will fix it up somehow or another

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Don't you scare yourself... We'll fix it up somehow or another.

events.label: John Ferrier tells his daughter that Jefferson will be messaged to come from Nevada and advise them

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: There's a party starting for Nevada to-morrow, and I'll manage to send him a message letting him know the hole we are in. If I know anything o' that young man, he'll be back here with a speed that would whip electro-telegraphs. When he comes, he will advise us for the best. But it is for you that I am frightened, dear.

events.label: John Ferrier's daughter objects and John Ferrier says they have time and will leave Utah at the end of the month

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: It will be time to look out for squalls when we do... We have a clear month before us; at the end of that, I guess we had best shin out of Utah.

events.label: John Ferrier says they will raise money for the farm and that he has considered leaving before

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: We will raise as much as we can in money, and let the rest go. To tell the truth, Lucy, it isn't the first time I have thought of doing it.

events.label: John Ferrier states he is a free-born American and warns that resisting prophet orders could lead to violence

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: I don't care about knuckling under to any man, as these folk do to their darned prophet... I'm a free-born American... Guess I'm too old to learn. If he comes browsing about this farm, he might chance to run up against a charge of buckshot travelling in the opposite direction.

events.label: John Ferrier reassures his daughter about leaving Utah while preparing the doors and loading the shotgun that night

communicates.speaker: john_ferrier
communicates.content: Wait till Jefferson comes, and we'll soon manage that... There's nothing to be afeared about, and there's no danger at all.

clues.significance: Holmes pointed to a lit candle on the mantelpiece to explain why the blood-red word RACHE was written in the brightest corner rather than the darkest corner of the wall.

Holmes inferred from the cab having made two ruts near the curb, along with the lack of rain for a week and the cab being there after rain began, that the cab (and therefore the two individuals) had been at the house during the night.
Holmes inferred from horse hoof marks indicating one was newly shod that the cab brought the two individuals to the house during the night.

Watson inferred that the writing on the wall was made with a man's forefinger dipped in blood from the plaster being slightly scratched in the process and the absence of such scratching if the man's nail had been trimmed.
Watson inferred from the dark, flaky ash taken from the floor that it was ash only made by a Trichinopoly.
Watson inferred a connection between the second man and writing the German word 'RACHE' immediately before decamping, as part of reconciling multiple facts of the mystery.

Holmes inferred that the German word involved was not written by a German because the letter 'A' was printed somewhat after the German fashion, whereas a real German would invariably print in Latin character.
Holmes received an answer to his American telegram, affecting his course of action in the Brixton Road wedding-ring matter (past-tense account given by Holmes in-scene).
Gregson used the hat sent to Mr. Drebber at Charpentier's Boarding Establishment to get Drebber's address
Gregson referred to the writing on the wall as part of the set of items that could be used to mislead police
Holmes pointed to the word RACHE written in letters of blood as evidence above the murdered man.
Lestrade reported that a small chip ointment box on the window-sill contained a couple of pills.
Holmes used the terrier to test which of the pills was poisonous, resulting in the terrier dying after receiving the second dissolved pill.
Jefferson Hope found a newly-dug grave marker with a paper stating John Ferrier’s death date, and treated it as the only epitaph for the missing old man.
